claim: The amine blocks have a fixed left-to-right order.
locus_b: Table S2 (SI p. 39) block headers and Fig. S3A/S3B x-axis groups: 70, 75, 80, 96, 400, 113, 414, 616, 110, T3A
what_we_emitted: Values keyed on each column's printed LABEL, never on its position. Measured and recorded in 07_qc.json -> P5b_amine_column_order_S1_vs_S2 (orders_agree = false, positions 3 and 4).
why: Table S1 is the odd one out: 96 and 400 are swapped relative to BOTH other loci. Every column in both tables is labelled in full, so the discrepancy costs nothing as long as the read is label-driven -- but a positional read would move ten Library-1 values between amine 96 and amine 400 and nothing downstream could see it.

claim: Table S1's values are reported at a uniform precision.
locus_a: Table S1: 45 of 50 cells are bare integers (30, 193, 663, ... 1953)
locus_b: Table S1: the five cells of the `113` column, and only those, carry one decimal -- 503.9, 848.5, 305.9, 349.5, 152.3
what_we_emitted: Both as printed. No rounding, no re-scaling.
why: One column of 50 cells being reported to an extra significant figure is the signature of a column produced or pasted separately from the rest. It is not a value error and we have no way to resolve it from the paper, but it is the kind of thing that precedes one: amine 113 is the lead compound's amine, and its column is the one that was handled differently.

locus_a: 10 amines x 5 epoxides = 50; Table S1 holds exactly 50 values; Fig. S3A draws 50 bars in ten groups of five.
locus_b: Fig. S7 caption, twice: "the hemolysis rates of the 52 lipids" and "The hemolysis rate of 52 lipids (n = 3)"
what_we_emitted: 50 Library-1 structures and 50 Library-1 values. Nothing from Fig. S7 is emitted.
why: 52 is most plausibly 50 library members plus two benchmark LNPs, but the caption says "lipids" both times and names no controls. Unresolvable from the SI; recorded so that a later reader does not take 52 as the library size.

locus_a: Fig. S3 caption: "Cytotoxicity of LNPs in Library 1 and 2"; both y axes read "Cytotoxicity (%)"
locus_b: The same panels' titles read "The cellular activity of LNP in Library 1 / 2"; the plotted values run from ~80 to ~220 percent with a dashed reference line at 80%
what_we_emitted: Nothing. No Fig. S3 value is emitted.
why: A quantity that exceeds 100% and whose acceptance threshold is a LOWER bound at 80% is relative cell VIABILITY, not cytotoxicity. The axis label and the panel title contradict each other and the data's own scale agrees with the title. Recorded because anyone pooling "cytotoxicity" across papers on the axis label alone would invert this one.

claim: The acyl block has one name.
locus_a: Table S2 row labels: Cl6, Cl8, Cl10, Cl12, Cl14
locus_b: Compound names elsewhere (Fig. S3B axis "70-AA-C8C6", and the lead "113-AA-C8C14") write the same block as C6 ... C14
what_we_emitted: Joined through an explicit map (ROW_TO_ACYL in stage05_values.py) rather than by string surgery, and the join is validated by the lead-compound check.
why: Purely nomenclatural, but the entire Library-2 name reconstruction depends on it: `Cl` is the acid chloride, `C` is the acyl group it leaves. If the two were conflated the names would not match the enumeration, which is why 05_values.csv asserts a 1:1 map onto the 300 enumerated structures.

claim: Library 1 and Library 2 are reported on one scale.
locus_b: Table S2 (Library 2): range 150 - 98,000, median 1,100 -- about 50x higher at the top end
what_we_emitted: A single pooled z-score of log10 over all 300 values (value_normalization_unit = experiment).
why: Not a contradiction in the data, but the decision it forces is real and is queued as DECISIONS.md D-2. The two tables share NO compound, so nothing anchors them to each other; pooling preserves the between-library difference the paper's narrative rests on, splitting deletes it. QL_2026 is the precedent in both directions: separate standardisation there erased a 37x library difference and inverted 36% of cross-library pairs while every check still passed.
